findings_to_judge.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SWBI's exact fiscal Q1 (May+June+July 2026) totalled 3,290,647 against 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.70% y/y - a 6.5-point acceleration from the +1.20% in the Feb-Apr quarter on which SWBI just printed revenue +26.7% and handgun sell-in +23.2%, while consensus looks for only +16% revenue growth off an $85.1M base.

Both channel layers turned positive in SWBI's exact quarter, and both datapoints were published after SWBI last spoke: Ruger's distributor inventories fell 45,800 units and finished goods 100,100 units on sell-through +19% (2026-07-29), and Sportsman's Warehouse's 10-Q for the 13 weeks ended 2026-08-01 shows firearm sales +$5.2M / +8.7% and ammunition +$3.9M / +9.9% (filed 2026-09-01).

On 2026-08-05 the N.D. Texas entered final judgment and a permanent injunction in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF holding NFA registration of suppressors/SBRs/SBSs unconstitutional after the tax went to zero; the stay expired 2026-08-12 and DOJ declined an emergency appeal - three weeks after SWBI's 2026-07-15 investor day told investors suppressors were its fastest-growing lane at +95.6% revenue growth in H1 CY2026 into a $700M-$950M TAM, with July NFA-category NICS checks +108.8% y/y to 130,013.

SWBI's Q1 FY27 guide of +15-20% revenue was given 2026-06-17 with only May adjusted NICS (+3.2% y/y) published; June came in +11.7% (1,123,006 vs 1,004,986) and July +8.5% (1,061,883 vs 978,731), so the two months the guide could not see were 3-4x stronger than the one it could, and the quarter-aligned May-July industry number is +7.7% y/y (3,290,647 vs 3,055,402).

NFA (suppressor/SBR) background checks are exploding after the 1-Jan-2026 elimination of the $200 tax stamp - June 2026 166,677 (+177.1% y/y) and July 2026 130,013 (+108.8%) - and SWBI's own Reg FD Investor Day deck filed 2026-07-15 discloses suppressor revenue +95.6% in the first six months of calendar 2026 against a US category it sizes at $700-950m; the June/July NFA data postdates the window that 95.6% covers, so the current run rate is higher than the only figure the company has published.

Sportsman's Warehouse reported its quarter ended 2026-08-01 on 2026-09-01 - two days before SWBI prints and covering almost exactly SWBI's May-July fiscal Q1 - with hunting and shooting sports same-store sales +6.7%, and CEO Paul Stone saying on the call 'Firearms up 8% and ammo is up nearly 11% on the Q'; the stock rose 9.2% after hours.

Ruger's 8-K for the coincident Apr-Jun 2026 quarter reports net sales $158.1m, +19% y/y, sell-through +19% against adjusted NICS +5%, and distributors' inventories down 45,800 units y/y - the channel manufacturers ship into is lean, which is the condition under which factory shipments run ahead of retail demand rather than behind it.

I can find no company-specific cause for the 16.4% 20-day de-rating: SWBI's only SEC filings since the 17-Jun print are a 7.01 investor-day deck (2026-07-15) and the routine FY26 annual report to shareholders (2026-08-06, a PDF-only submission), with zero Form 4s between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-03 and no 8-K under items 1.01, 2.03, 5.02 or 8.01.
